By Data Skrive ,
3 hours ago
On Thursday, looking for a series sweep, Julio Rodriguez and the Seattle Mariners (44-43) play the Los Angeles Angels (36-51), with first pitch scheduled for 9:40 p.m. ET at T-Mobile Park.
Keep reading to find out how to watch the Seattle-Los Angeles matchup below.
When is Mariners vs. Angels and when does it start? This matchup between the Mariners and Angels will take place on Thursday, July 2, 2026. You can expect the opening pitch at 9:40 p.m. ET.
Where to watch Mariners vs. Angels The Mariners and Angels will hit the diamond at T-Mobile Park for this matchup on July 2, and if you’d like to see the matchup live, get your tickets now from Vivid Seats !
What channel is the game on? You can catch this game live on Mariners.TV and ABTV.
Watch the Mariners vs. Angels live stream on Fubo Live Stream Online: Sign up for Fubo today!
Mariners vs. Angels Game Preview These clubs meet again following the Mariners’ 8-3 victory over the Angels Tuesday. Bryan Woo (6.1 IP, 2 R, 4 H, 5 K) picked up the win for the Mariners. Colt Emerson went 3 for 4 with two RBIs to lead the team on offense. Jose Soriano (5.0 IP, 3 R, 6 H, 9 K) was credited with the loss on the mound for the Angels.
Mariners Stats, Odds & Insights The Mariners have compiled a 41-36 record in games they were favored on the moneyline (winning 53.2% of those games).
Seattle ranks 11th in MLB action with 105 home runs. They average 1.2 per game.
The Mariners have the fifth-lowest slugging percentage in baseball (.384).
Seattle has a 3.70 team ERA that ranks fifth across all MLB pitching staffs.
The Mariners have the fourth-lowest WHIP in baseball (1.192).
Angels Stats, Odds & Insights The Angels have been underdogs in 69 games this season and won 27 (39.1%) of those contests.
Los Angeles has hit 101 homers this season, which ranks 15th in the majors.
The Angels are 18th in MLB with a slugging percentage of .396 this season.
Los Angeles pitchers have a combined ERA of 4.65 ERA this year, which ranks 25th in MLB.
The Angels have a combined 1.408 WHIP as a pitching staff, fifth-highest in MLB.

He is 3-2 with a 1.97 ERA and 54 strikeouts in 45 2/3 innings pitched.
His last appearance was on Thursday against the Pittsburgh Pirates, when the righty threw 5 2/3 innings, surrendering three earned runs while allowing five hits.
The 27-year-old has put up an ERA of 1.97, with 10.6 strikeouts per nine innings, in eight games this season. Opponents have a .178 batting average against him.
Rodriguez leads Seattle in home runs this season with 14 while driving in 40 runs.
Randy Arozarena is batting .283 to lead Seattle, while adding eight homers and 37 runs batted in this season.
Josh Naylor has 81 hits this season and a slash line of .257/.321/.368.
Angels Key Players to Watch The Angels will send Walbert Urena (5-6) to the mound for his 14th start this season.
The right-hander last pitched on Saturday, when he gave up seven earned runs and allowed six hits in 4 1/3 innings against the Athletics.
The 22-year-old has an ERA of 3.14, a 1.86 strikeout-to-walk ratio and a WHIP of 1.340 in 15 games this season.
Zach Neto has launched a team-best 18 home runs.
Jo Adell’s 45 runs batted in are a team-high mark.
Nolan Schanuel paces the Angels with a .262 batting average.
